items.response: Understood, reverting the whoami change; it was never committed. Action: restore the whoami file to its original loop, confirm with git status that the working tree is clean for it, and leave the org display for you to rethink.

Will do. The dialog title, description and the confirm button will say 'Archive customer' instead of delete, and I'll update the trigger button too. I'll keep the copy free of exclamation marks. Action: edit the DeleteCustomerButton copy, leave the deleteCustomer action and soft-delete behavior as they are unless you want them renamed, and run the web tests.

Leaving the dist file as is. For export: failures will go to Sentry with the DSN from SENTRY_DSN, and the command goes behind a GrowthBook flag, and I need the flag key from you since it has to be created there too. I'll add a Vitest snapshot test of the csv stdout. For the stash, I won't use git stash: I'll look at what it holds, move that work onto the branch as a commit, and ask before dropping it. Action: git stash list and show the contents, then do the Sentry, flag and snapshot test work.

Will do. slugify will lowercase, strip punctuation and collapse whitespace to hyphens, so 'Northwind Studio, Inc.' gives 'northwind-studio-inc'. I'll use a named export, not a default export, and Vitest for the tests. Action: create packages/cli/src/util/slug.ts and slug.test.ts with that case plus a few edge cases (accents, repeated spaces, leading and trailing punctuation), then run the cli tests.

I don't know how the api is exposed, and I'd rather not give you a guess to repeat to Priya. Let me read the infra to find out. Action: check infra for the ingress, load balancer and cert setup (helm ingress, Terraform, cert-manager or ACM), and give you a short plain explanation including how the cert gets renewed.

The jumping is from proportional digit widths, and a monospace font fixes it. But `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` (Tailwind's tabular-nums) gives equal digit widths in the current font with no new font to load. Action: find the invoice number and amount columns in the tables, apply tabular-nums there, and show you; if you still want JetBrains Mono I'll check how fonts are loaded and add it.

Clerk is the auth provider, and social login is switched on in the Clerk dashboard under the social connections settings for the right instance (production, not dev). I can't see the dashboard from here, so you'd need to check that Google is enabled; a vanished button could also come from a code change in the sign-in page. Action: check git log for yesterday's changes to the sign-in page and its Clerk config, and tell you what I find.

I don't have any memory of yesterday in this session, so I'll rebuild it from the repo. Action: check the current branch, git status, recent commits, stashes and open PRs, and summarize where things stand.

Turborepo is already in use with pipelines in turbo.json, so the fix is mostly using it properly in CI. That means running only affected packages (turbo's --filter with a git base ref, which needs enough git history fetched), declaring inputs and outputs in turbo.json, and enabling remote caching so runs reuse results. Action: read the CI workflow and turbo.json, then propose the changes, including path filters for docs-only changes; I'll ask which remote cache backend you want.

Using what I know: Postgres 16, money in integer cents, timestamps in UTC, and rows soft-deleted via deleted_at, so the query will filter out deleted rows and keep totals as integer cents. I need the real table and column names, so I'll read the schema first. Action: check the schema for invoices (org id, status, total, paid timestamp), then write tools/sql/ monthly revenue rollup with sum per org per month over the last 12 months and a running total per org using a window function.

I don't know where they end up, so let me check instead of guessing. Action: look at the worker's metrics setup, the helm chart and monitoring config for how metrics are scraped and which Grafana datasource reads them, and find whether a billing-sync queue depth metric exists. Then I'll tell you the path and build the panel.

Back on acme: that usually means the dropdown has no outside-click handler, or its overlay is not dismissable. Action: find the org switcher component, check whether it is a Radix or other primitive with an open state or a hand-rolled dropdown, fix the outside-click close, and add a test.

Good call, since kind already means one-off vs recurring on invoice. I'll rename only the badge prop and leave invoice.kind alone. Action: rename the prop on InvoiceStatusBadge to status using the TypeScript rename, update every call site, then run typecheck and the web tests.

Before the PR I'll test the command end to end against the real API, not just the unit tests. Since you added cli-table3, I'll check pnpm-lock.yaml is committed because CI uses --frozen-lockfile, and run pnpm changeset since this is a user-facing change. Also never deploy to prod on a Friday, so I'll check that the 9th isn't one. Action: run acme invoices list and acme invoices list --json piped to jq, commit with a Conventional Commits message (feat(cli): ...) in imperative mood with a short body, then open the PR.

There's already app/global-error.tsx reporting to Sentry, so I'll build on that and add a route-level fallback with a 'try again' button that calls reset(), so a render error on the reports page doesn't white-screen the app. Action: on branch acme-447, add the fallback error page, keep the Sentry reporting, test it by throwing in a component, then commit with a Conventional Commits message (fix(web): ...) in imperative mood with a short body explaining why.
